rootEtymology: pra + √kāś (to shine forth intensely, to illuminate)
conciseDefinition: The self-luminous, unconditioned light of pure Consciousness that reveals all existence. Without Prakāśa, nothing could ever appear or be known.
advaitaContrast: In Classical Advaita, Brahman is static, passive luminescence without self-awareness. In Trika, Prakāśa is never inert (jaḍa); it is eternally coupled with active self-reflection (Vimarśa).

rootEtymology: vi + √mṛś (to touch, reflect upon, actively scrutinize)
conciseDefinition: The dynamic, kinetic self-awareness and reflective agency inherent in Consciousness. It is the power by which Consciousness knows itself: 'I am Śiva'.
advaitaContrast: Advaita rejects internal dynamism in Nirguṇa Brahman as Māyā. Trika maintains Vimarśa is the very life-pulse (spanda) of Reality; without Vimarśa, Prakāśa would be as unconscious as a crystal mirror or a stone.

rootEtymology: sva (self) + tantra (rule/web) + ya (state of being self-ruled)
conciseDefinition: Absolute sovereign freedom and unconditioned autonomy of Consciousness to manifest anything out of its own essence without any external material or instrument.
advaitaContrast: In Advaita, world creation requires an extrinsic illusory principle (Māyā). In Trika, the universe is the glorious, unforced free expression (Svātantrya-Śakti) of Consciousness delighting in itself.

conciseDefinition: The subtle divine pulsation of Consciousness that perpetually opens (Unmeṣa) and closes (Nimeṣa), projecting and withdrawing the universe while remaining unmoving.
advaitaContrast: Advaita views change as unreal illusion (Vivarta). Trika views dynamic vibration as the inherent ecstasy and creative reality (Pariṇāma-free Spanda) of the Supreme Subject.

rootEtymology: ā + √bhās (to shine toward, appear forth, radiate)
conciseDefinition: The flash or appearance of an objective manifestation within Consciousness. Every sensation, thought, and object is an Ābhāsa illuminated on the mirror of the Self.
advaitaContrast: Advaita calls appearances false illusions (Mithyā). Trika's Ābhāsavāda proves appearances are real expressions of divine Light—the world is literally God appearing as forms.

rootEtymology: kañc (to bind, tie, envelop) + uka (cloak, armor)
conciseDefinition: The five cosmic cloaks (Kalā, Vidyā, Rāga, Kāla, Niyati) that contract the Lord's five absolute powers into limited human experience.
advaitaContrast: In Advaita, ignorance is an inexplicable, single Avidyā. In Trika, the Kañcukas are an exact architectural descent through which the Infinite intentionally experiences finitude.

conciseDefinition: The cloak and psychological craving born from perceived incompleteness (Āṇava Mala), compelling the contracted soul to seek satisfaction in external forms.
advaitaContrast: In Advaita, desire is a mental defect to be eradicated; in Trika, Rāga is an ontological contraction of the Lord's absolute Fullness (Pūrṇatva) that is redeemed when desire is redirected to its source.

rootEtymology: aṇu (atomic particle, contracted point) + mala (stain, veil)
conciseDefinition: The innate metaphysical contraction wherein Consciousness forgets its infinite nature and experiences an agonizing sense of lack, smallness, and limitation.
advaitaContrast: Advaita views bondage as cognitive superimposition (Adhyāsa). Trika views Āṇava Mala as an ontological voluntary contraction of divine Svātantrya requiring energetic recognition (Pratyabhijñā).

conciseDefinition: The impurity of seeing differentiation and duality: perceiving the world as outside of, different from, and opposed to one's own conscious Self.
advaitaContrast: Unlike Advaita which dismisses duality as non-existent, Trika treats this as a perceptual contraction to be reabsorbed into pure non-dual oneness.

conciseDefinition: The impurity of bound agency that believes 'I am the individual doer of actions, subject to good and bad karma and reward/punishment'.
advaitaContrast: In Trika, when actions are dedicated and experienced as the divine movement of Śakti, karma dissolves immediately into Spanda.

conciseDefinition: Discursive, dichotomizing conceptual thought that operates by distinguishing 'this' from 'not-this', dividing experience into categories.
advaitaContrast: Advaita advocates complete suppression of thought (Nirvikalpa Samādhi). Trika purifies thought (Śuddhavikalpa) so that thought itself becomes a vehicle for realizing Shiva.

conciseDefinition: The non-conceptual, immediate awareness that directly tastes the essence of Reality before linguistic categories and mental labeling intervene.
advaitaContrast: In Trika, Nirvikalpa is not a trance where the world is erased, but the fresh, direct recognition of Consciousness pulsating within all vibrant moments.

rootEtymology: khe (in the sky / void of pure Consciousness) + carī (moving, roaming)
conciseDefinition: The state or mudrā of soaring freely in the open sky of Consciousness. In internal practice, it represents the dissolution of mind in the infinite space of the Heart.
advaitaContrast: Not merely a physical tongue-inversion as in Haṭha Yoga, but the supreme existential altitude where the yogi roams as Universal Consciousness.

rootEtymology: cakra (wheel of sensory and cosmic energies) + īśvara (lord, master)
conciseDefinition: The Master of the Wheel of Powers. One who is no longer dragged along by the senses, but commands their inward illumination as sovereign sovereign.
advaitaContrast: Advaita seeks detachment from the senses; Trika transforms the senses into a radiant retinue of goddesses serving the Master.

conciseDefinition: The central focal point or gap between two states—between inhalation and exhalation, between two thoughts, between waking and sleeping.
advaitaContrast: The foundational contemplative doorway of the Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra; resting in the gap reveals the unconditioned essence of Bhairava.

rootEtymology: ud + √miṣ (to open one's eyes, blossom, awaken)
conciseDefinition: The outward emergence of manifestation, or internally, the spontaneous flashing open of divine awareness when external perception relaxes.
advaitaContrast: Unmeṣa shows that manifestation and liberation are complementary phases of one living pulse rather than an irreconcilable contradiction.

rootEtymology: ni + √miṣ (to close the eyes, contract inward)
conciseDefinition: The withdrawal or reabsorption of external objective display back into the silent interior of Consciousness.
advaitaContrast: When objective world withdraws (Nimeṣa of world), inner divine light blossoms (Unmeṣa of Śiva)—they occur simultaneously.

rootEtymology: prati (back, toward) + abhi (facing directly) + √jñā (to know, recognize)
conciseDefinition: Spontaneous re-cognition: realizing 'I, who previously felt finite and helpless, am in truth that very omnipotent Supreme Lord Śiva'.
advaitaContrast: Unlike the Advaita metaphor of the rope and snake (illusion removal), Pratyabhijñā is the romantic recognition of a beloved king whose treasures were already yours.

conciseDefinition: Consciousness in its active, creative feminine aspect as the supreme Goddess who generates, sustains, and withdraws the entire cosmos on Her own canvas.
advaitaContrast: Brahman in Advaita is grammatically neuter and functionally passive. In Trika, Citi is sovereign, free, and intentionally creative.

rootEtymology: camat (a joyful exclamation of wonder) + kāra (making, producing)
conciseDefinition: The ecstasy of aesthetic wonder and blissful tasting of one's own conscious nature in any intense experience.
advaitaContrast: Aesthetics and non-dual yoga are identical in Abhinavagupta's Trika; mystical realization is the highest rasa of Camatkāra.

conciseDefinition: The foundational state of pure witness consciousness that underlies and pervades the three ordinary states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
advaitaContrast: Advaita treats Turya as an isolated witness. Trika infuses Turya into all waking activity so everyday life becomes continuous contemplation.

conciseDefinition: The state beyond the fourth, wherein even the distinction between the witness and the witnessed disappears into all-pervasive nectar.
advaitaContrast: The pinnacle of Kashmir Shaiva immersion where no trace of duality or detachment remains; the entire universe is tasted as one continuous divine ambrosia.

conciseDefinition: The direct realization that Consciousness is already fully enlightened and unconfined, requiring zero techniques or progressive steps.
advaitaContrast: The ultimate view of Trika: that looking for a path to Śiva assumes you are currently away from Śiva, which is impossible.

conciseDefinition: The non-conceptual path of sovereign Will (Icchā) where the aspirant drops all mental formulations and directly plunges into the unconstructed presence of the Self.
advaitaContrast: Transfers attention instantly into the source of awareness without using sensory objects or mental mantras.

conciseDefinition: The cognitive path of discerning Knowledge (Jñāna) where divisive thoughts are pierced and purified into continuous contemplation of the Divine (Śuddhavikalpa).
advaitaContrast: Instead of suppressing thought, it uses the reflective nature of thought to ride the energy back to its conscious wellspring.

conciseDefinition: The progressive sensory path of Action (Kriyā) employing breath (Prāṇa), body (Karaṇa), sound (Ucchāra), and sensory gates to lead the mind to stillness.
advaitaContrast: Provides concrete, physical contemplative anchors for beginners who cannot yet stabilize in purely non-conceptual awareness.

conciseDefinition: The sonic power of the Sanskrit alphabet (from A to Kṣa) that unconsciously shapes human cognition, binding the bound soul into linguistic traps and anxiety.
advaitaContrast: Trika provides an advanced sonic ontology: language is not mere conventional tool, but a divine matrix that binds when misunderstood and liberates when decoded.

rootEtymology: mālā (garland) + inī (she who wears the garland of phonemes)
conciseDefinition: The esoteric, non-linear arrangement of Sanskrit letters (Na to Pha) symbolizing the non-sequential, liberating power of the supreme Goddess.
advaitaContrast: The supreme Tantric sonic key used in Kṣemarāja and Abhinavagupta's highest ritual and contemplative invocations.

conciseDefinition: The dynamic multitude of manifest forms, the physical body, and the field of sensory powers viewed as an interconnected divine family.
advaitaContrast: In Advaita, the body is an obstacle to be discarded. In Kula Tantra, the body is the supreme temple and instrument of divine awakening.

conciseDefinition: The transcendent, unmanifest source (Śiva) beyond all physical and metaphysical family forms.
advaitaContrast: Trika emphasizes the uninterrupted union (Sāmarasya) of Akula (Śiva) and Kula (Śakti).

conciseDefinition: The temporal sequence of cosmic and cognitive phases through which Consciousness creates, sustains, dissolves, and transcends all events.
advaitaContrast: Krama worships the cycles of time and cognitive dissolution (the 12 Kālīs) as doorways into the timeless.

rootEtymology: sam (together, completely) + ā (fully) + √viś (to enter, penetrate, absorb)
conciseDefinition: Complete mystical absorption and interpenetration wherein the individual sense of identity dissolves entirely into the divine energy of Śiva.
advaitaContrast: Not an intellectual assent, but an overwhelming, visceral somatic immersion into God-consciousness.

conciseDefinition: Spiritual liberation while continuing to live fully in the physical body, enjoying the world as the play of divine Consciousness.
advaitaContrast: In Advaita, the world is tolerated until physical death. In Trika, Jīvanmukti is an active celebration of embodied divinity (Bhoga and Mokṣa united).

rootEtymology: ud + √yam (to rise up, surge forward, exert)
conciseDefinition: The sudden spontaneous upsurge of divine awareness that instantly obliterates all psychological lethargy and duality (Śiva Sūtra 1.5).
advaitaContrast: Direct lightning awakening: catching the initial surge of energy before it fragments into mental doubt.

conciseDefinition: The creative emission or outflowing of Consciousness into objective manifestation, symbolized by the two vertical dots of the Sanskrit aspirate ḥ.
advaitaContrast: Emphasizes that God does not create out of obligation or necessity, but overflows with irresistible love and self-delight.

rootEtymology: A (first Sanskrit vowel, Śiva) + Ha (last consonant, Śakti) + Bindu (m, integration)
conciseDefinition: The supreme, uncontracted I-Consciousness containing the entire spectrum of cosmic vibrations from A to Ha.
advaitaContrast: Advaita negates the 'I' to reach the impersonal Self. Trika elevates 'Aham' to its supreme, divine fullness as the living Subject of all worlds.

conciseDefinition: The objective universe as perceived or held in relation to the subjective 'I' (Aham).
advaitaContrast: In early stages, 'Idam' seems separate; in realized Trika, 'Idam' is realized to be identical to 'Aham' ('I am This universe').

conciseDefinition: The intentional contraction by which infinite Consciousness assumes finite dimensions, thoughts, and bodies.
advaitaContrast: Contraction is not a flaw or tragic accident, but a marvelous divine artifice through which God plays hide-and-seek with Himself.

conciseDefinition: The glorious expansion and opening of Consciousness to reclaim its native universality.
advaitaContrast: The complementary movement to Saṅkoca, marking the path of spiritual return.

conciseDefinition: The five continuous divine acts of Consciousness: Sṛṣṭi (emanation), Sthiti (maintenance), Saṃhāra (dissolution), Tirodhāna (concealment), and Anugraha (grace).
advaitaContrast: In Trika, even the human individual is performing these exact five acts in every momentary perception (Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam Sūtra 10).

conciseDefinition: The manifestation and shining forth of thoughts, sensations, and cosmic phenomena into objective appearance.
advaitaContrast: Creation is an act of divine radiance rather than an illusory mistake.

conciseDefinition: The steady holding and savoring of an experience in the light of awareness.
advaitaContrast: Maintenance is the preservation of appearances through conscious attention.

conciseDefinition: The reabsorption of objective thoughts and worlds back into the undifferentiated silent Heart of Consciousness.
advaitaContrast: Dissolution is welcomed as the blissful return home to pure rest.

conciseDefinition: The divine act of concealment through which the Lord hides His infinite identity behind the mask of human individuality.
advaitaContrast: Veiling is an intentional divine artifice, not an independent, beginningless Avidyā.

conciseDefinition: The spontaneous bestowal of divine Grace and spiritual awakening (Śaktipāta) that turns the heart inward toward liberation.
advaitaContrast: Grace is the sovereign, unearned initiative of Consciousness recognizing itself in its own creation.

rootEtymology: paś (to look, perceive externally) or pāśa (tether, rope)
conciseDefinition: The bound soul; consciousness tethered by the ropes (Pāśa) of the three Malas and the five Kañcukas.
advaitaContrast: The Paśu is not fundamentally distinct from Śiva; it is Śiva Himself looking out through contracted lenses.

conciseDefinition: The sovereign Lord of Awareness who is eternally free, unconditioned, and the master of all cosmic powers.
advaitaContrast: In Śaiva Siddhānta, Pati, Paśu, and Pāśa are eternally three separate realities. In Trika, Paśu and Pāśa are only contracted expressions of Pati.

conciseDefinition: The fetters and tethers (Malas, Kañcukas, karmic residues) that bind the infinite Lord into the conditioned state of a creature.
advaitaContrast: Fetters are made of the Lord's own energy and are untied through the flash of Recognition.

conciseDefinition: The six cosmic courses (Ṣaḍadhvan) through which Consciousness descends and ascends: 3 sonic paths (Varṇa, Pada, Mantra) and 3 objective paths (Kalā, Tattva, Bhuvana).
advaitaContrast: A comprehensive cosmological map integrating linguistics, subtle architecture, and geography into the body of the Divine.

conciseDefinition: The metaphor of piercing 100 stacked lotus leaves with a single thrust of a needle: though an infinitesimal sequence exists, the awakening appears instantaneous.
advaitaContrast: Explains how the progressive paths collapse into instantaneous enlightenment at the moment of grace.

conciseDefinition: The self-delighting, completely autonomous spontaneity of Consciousness that answers to no external master or law.
advaitaContrast: Svacchanda expresses the joyful wildness and playful freedom of Bhairava.

conciseDefinition: The uncaused, unconditional bliss of Consciousness resting in its own boundless nature.
advaitaContrast: Not the absence of suffering (as in Nyāya), but a positive, thrilling taste of divine nectar vibrating in all things.

conciseDefinition: The divine sovereign Will of Consciousness to create and project manifestation.
advaitaContrast: Desire in Advaita is a source of bondage; in Trika, pure divine Icchā is the sacred prime mover of cosmic existence.

conciseDefinition: The cognitive power of Consciousness that surveys, comprehends, and illuminates all things.
advaitaContrast: Contracted knowledge is bondage (SS.1.2: Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ); supreme non-dual knowledge is liberation.

conciseDefinition: The power of creative action through which Consciousness brings forth forms and structures in the world.
advaitaContrast: In Advaita, Brahman is Akartā (non-doer). In Trika, Kartṛtva (absolute doership) is the defining attribute of the Supreme Lord.

conciseDefinition: Authentic, ultimate reality; the luminous presence of Shiva underlying all appearances.
advaitaContrast: Points to the tangible, positive presence of Reality rather than a bare negation.

rootEtymology: sama (equal, same) + rasa (flavor, juice, essence) + ya
conciseDefinition: Equanimity of equal flavor: the complete, ecstatic reconciliation where Śiva and Śakti, transcendence and immanence, are tasted as one indivisible nectar.
advaitaContrast: The world is not sublated or abandoned; it is tasted with the exact same divine flavor as pure Consciousness.

conciseDefinition: Any entity, object, state of being, or emotional feeling that appears within awareness.
advaitaContrast: Every Bhāva is an opportunity for contemplation, serving as a portal back into pure consciousness.

conciseDefinition: Absence, voidness, or emptiness; used in contemplative sādhana as a doorway to step out of mental clutter into pure space.
advaitaContrast: Abhāva is not sheer nothingness, but the unencumbered openness of pure awareness (Vyoma).

conciseDefinition: The primordial evolutionary and spiritual life-force coiled at the base of the subtle body; in Trika, it is Cit-Kuṇḍalinī, Consciousness itself awakening in the spinal pathway (Suṣumnā).
advaitaContrast: Understood not merely as a biological energy, but as the supreme Goddess reabsorbing all contracted faculties back into the Crown of Shiva.

conciseDefinition: The harmonization and equalization of the vital breath currents (Prāṇa and Apāna) into the central channel (Madhya / Suṣumnā).
advaitaContrast: The practical physiological key in Kashmir Shaivism that stills mental fluctuations and awakens non-dual recognition.

conciseDefinition: The radiant Spiritual Heart: not the anatomical muscle, but the infinite, all-encompassing center of pure Consciousness where the universe pulses.
advaitaContrast: The womb and resting place of all creation; resting in the Heart is the heart of Trika realization.

rootEtymology: √bind (to split, concentrate into a drop, point)
conciseDefinition: The dimensionless focal point of concentrated consciousness and creative potential; the drop of illumination ready to expand.
advaitaContrast: Symbolizes the intense condensation of Śiva-Śakti prior to cosmic projection.

conciseDefinition: The primal, unstruck acoustic vibration (Anāhata) that rings through Consciousness as the inner pulse of life.
advaitaContrast: Sound is treated as an ontological bridge between subtle energy and gross physical matter.

conciseDefinition: Resonance and poetic suggestion. In philosophy and poetics, the capacity of sound and word to convey unspoken transcendental meaning.
advaitaContrast: A cornerstone of Abhinavagupta's aesthetic and spiritual epistemology.

conciseDefinition: The infinite sky or void of Consciousness; the open, unconstructed space in which all thoughts and forms appear.
advaitaContrast: Meditating on open space or an empty vessel triggers spontaneous absorption into Consciousness.

conciseDefinition: The sacred transmission that expands (tanoti) the scope of consciousness and saves (trāyate) the aspirant from limitation.
advaitaContrast: Affirms the world, the senses, and the body as divine instruments of awakening, rejecting world-negating asceticism.

conciseDefinition: Spiritual initiation transmitted by a qualified Master that severs the bonds of ignorance and awakens the inner power of the disciple.
advaitaContrast: Required in historical Āgamic practice for formal ritual mantra work; distinguished from open universal contemplations.

conciseDefinition: The spiritual guide who embodies and awakens non-dual recognition in the student (Śiva Sūtra 2.6: Gurur upāyaḥ).
advaitaContrast: The Guru is not an external person to be worshipped idolatrously, but the living voice of one's own innermost Self (Śiva).

conciseDefinition: Disciplined, lineage-guided contemplative practice that stabilizes recognition in everyday life.
advaitaContrast: In Trika, sādhana is not an agonizing struggle to reach an absent God, but the joyous savoring of the Divine already present.

rootEtymology: Bha (nourishing, sustaining) + Ra (withdrawing, reabsorbing) + Va (emanating, projecting); or bhi-ru (fearsome to ignorance, terrifying to ego)
conciseDefinition: The supreme, fearless, all-pervading non-dual Consciousness that perpetually creates, sustains, and reabsorbs the entire cosmos.
advaitaContrast: Not an angry mythological deity, but the fierce, tender totality of pure Awareness unconfined by polite social dualisms.

rootEtymology: Feminine form of Bhairava; the supreme consort and kinetic energy of Bhairava
conciseDefinition: The dynamic creative power through which Bhairava knows Himself and unfolds the manifest universe.
advaitaContrast: Bhairava and Bhairavī are as inseparable as fire and heat, water and wetness.

conciseDefinition: Absolute Consciousness in its pristine, uncreated, self-existent nature.
advaitaContrast: Cit is both the witness and the dynamic substance of everything appearing before it.

rootEtymology: cetana (sentient being) + -ya (the essential nature of consciousness)
conciseDefinition: Sentient, living, sovereign Consciousness (Śiva Sūtra 1.1: Caitanayam ātmā - Consciousness is the true Self).
advaitaContrast: Defines the Self not as a passive blank screen, but as an actively knowing, free sovereign agent.

conciseDefinition: The Great Sovereign Lord who commands all universal powers and holds cosmic totality within Himself.
advaitaContrast: Affirms the majestic, active sovereignty of the Supreme Being.

conciseDefinition: The absolute non-dual Reality that transcends and encompasses both the manifest and the unmanifest, both Śiva and Śakti.
advaitaContrast: Beyond even the distinction of static light and dynamic energy; the ultimate synthesis of all existence.

conciseDefinition: The spontaneous flash of intuitive wisdom and artistic/philosophical genius that illuminates the truth directly without intermediate reasoning.
advaitaContrast: Treated as the supreme voice of the Goddess guiding the practitioner from within.

conciseDefinition: The quality of clarity, luminosity, peace, and transparency in mental nature.
advaitaContrast: The primary psychological vehicle through which divine reflection is clearly received.

conciseDefinition: The quality of motion, passion, agitation, ambition, and kinetic drive in nature.
advaitaContrast: Powers action and desire, driving either outward distraction or inward intense spiritual longing.

conciseDefinition: The quality of inertia, sleep, ignorance, obstruction, and resistance in nature.
advaitaContrast: The density that condenses subtle thought into tangible physical matter and bodily form.

conciseDefinition: The tripartite inner cognitive instrument consisting of Buddhi (intellect), Ahaṅkāra (ego-sense), and Manas (processing mind).
advaitaContrast: The mirror through which the Lord views and operates within the physical organism.

conciseDefinition: The five subtle elemental essences (sound, touch, form, taste, smell) that precede gross physical elements.
advaitaContrast: The vibrational bridge between subjective perception and objective physical reality.

conciseDefinition: The five gross elements (Ether, Air, Fire, Water, Earth) that constitute physical matter and bodily forms.
advaitaContrast: Regarded as the outer condensed skin of Consciousness itself.

conciseDefinition: One's authentic, intrinsic essential nature as pure uncontracted Consciousness.
advaitaContrast: Recognizing Svarūpa is the culmination of all Trika study.

conciseDefinition: The innate, spontaneous, natural state of being awake without contrivance or forced ascetic posture.
advaitaContrast: Emphasizes that enlightenment is not an unnatural manufactured trance, but your innate original reality.

conciseDefinition: Ever-arisen, continuously shining; awareness that never sets, never sleeps, and never vanishes (Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam Sūtra 19).
advaitaContrast: Assures the seeker that samādhi is not something you enter and leave, but the ever-present ground of every breath.

conciseDefinition: The ineffable state beyond all linguistic categorization and cognitive labels; the supreme phase of the Krama cycle.
advaitaContrast: The mystery where even non-duality is transcended in sheer, unnamable presence.

conciseDefinition: Eternally unstained, pristine, and stainless; the natural purity of Consciousness that was never truly tarnished by the Malas.
advaitaContrast: Reminds the aspirant that purity does not need to be gained; it only needs to be recognized.

conciseDefinition: Astonished wonder: the primary ground and foundation of yogic realization (Śiva Sūtra 1.12: Vismayo yogabhūmikāḥ).
advaitaContrast: Instead of solemn seriousness, spiritual awakening is a state of fresh, wide-eyed astonishment at the miracle of existence.

conciseDefinition: The waking state of consciousness, defined in Śiva Sūtra 1.8 as ordinary fragmented knowledge (Jñānaṃ jāgrat).
advaitaContrast: Trika transforms waking into a continuous meditation by recognizing the objects as externalized light.

conciseDefinition: The dreaming state, characterized in Śiva Sūtra 1.9 as proliferating thoughts and mental imagery (Svapno vikalpāḥ).
advaitaContrast: The dream state demonstrates the mind's inherent power to create entire worlds without physical matter.

conciseDefinition: The deep, dreamless sleep state, defined in Śiva Sūtra 1.10 as lack of awareness and immersion in Māyā (Aviveko māyāsauṣuptam).
advaitaContrast: When consciousness maintains awareness in deep sleep, it awakens into unbroken Turya.
